---
title: "simstim host rm"
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Forget a host, and optionally delete its created machine.

```text
simstim host rm <host> [flags]
```

Removes a host from hosts.toml and cleans up its generated SSH config and pinned host key. On a host made by `host create`, at a terminal it asks whether to delete the machine too. Pass `--destroy` to delete the machine (and `--confirm` &lt;host&gt; when input is off). Refuses to delete a machine while a session is working unless `--force`.

## Examples

```sh
simstim host rm my-vps
simstim host rm my-vps --destroy --confirm my-vps
```

## Flags

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--confirm <string>` | type the host's name here instead of at the prompt (with `--destroy`) |
| `--destroy[=<host create>]` | delete the machine that host create made, then forget the host |
| `--force` | delete the machine even while a session is working (with `--destroy`) |

## Flags from the parent command

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--debug[=<categories>]` | turn on the debug mode, with every category, or with the categories listed: attach, net, memory, launcher, runtime. A list binds only in the = form, such as `--debug=net` |
| `--debug-file <file>` | write the client's debug records to this file. On its own, it turns on every category (SIMSTIM_DEBUG_FILE does the same) |
| `--no-color` | print no colour (NO_COLOR does the same) |
| `--no-input` | ask nothing: a question that needs an answer fails with exit code 4, and names the flag that answers it (SIMSTIM_NO_INPUT=1 does the same) |

## Old names

These still work, and print a warning on stderr, until their end.

| Old | New | Works until |
| --- | --- | --- |
| host destroy | host rm &lt;host&gt; --destroy | v0.4.0 and 11 November 2027, whichever comes later |
